name: Teriyaki Salmon Soba Noodle Bowl with Carrot, Bell Pepper, Cucumber & Cilantro (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Coat a baking sheet pan with a thin layer of oil.
Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap). Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.

While the water comes to a boil, pat the salmon dry with paper towels and cut into 3 portions. Transfer to the baking sheet and spread two portions with teriyaki sauce. Season the third portion with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 lb salmon fillet
teriyaki sauce & marinade
⅛ tsp salt
1 pinch black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until salmon is opaque and cooked through, 10-12 minutes. Remove from oven.
Once the water is boiling, add soba noodles and cook until tender, about 5 minutes (or cook according to package instructions). Drain and rinse in a colander; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ small bunch cilantro
1 medium carrot
1 English cucumber
½ red bell pepper

instructions.primary_message: Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Set aside for serving.
Place soy sauce, vinegar, oil, chili-garlic sauce, and honey in a medium bowl, then whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp rice vinegar
2 tsp toasted sesame oil
2 tsp chili-garlic sauce
honey

instructions.primary_message: Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot. Place a ¼-cup of grated carrot on a large plate, then add remaining carrot to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and small dice cucumber. Add a ⅓-cup of cucumber to the plate with the carrot, then add remaining cucumber to the bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add a ¼-cup of bell pepper to the plate, then add remaining bell pepper to the bowl.
Roughly chop 1 cup of plain noodles, add to the plate, and set aside for the kid plates. Add remaining whole noodles to the bowl, toss to combine, and set aside for the adult plates.
Place peanut butter, water, and honey in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the peanut sauce and set aside for the kid plates.
Break the plain portion of salmon into bite-sized pieces for the kid plates, discarding skin.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide grated carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, flaked salmon, and plain noodles between plates. Serve with peanut sauce on the side.

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide noodle salad and teriyaki salmon between bowls, then sprinkle with cilantro. Drizzle with additional teriyaki sauce (optional) and enjoy!
